description:
Keystone: the CRM seat can rewrite, re-identify, resume and run another user's accounting agents (AgentTask) - prompt, user_id and run history are all writable (HIGH)

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in; also Suryodaya] HIGH - cross-app privilege / audit integrity. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline, role sales_user, user 443778c5) with a READ-ONLY probe: tools/list and AgentTask.list only. Nothing was written.

What happened:
- AgentTask.list returns 2 tasks created by another user (created_by c91dd152-12e8-4595-b921-bad9fa347d43): 'Daily Invoice Reminder' (prompt: "Query all invoices with status 'sent' where the due date is more than 7 days ago...") and 'Weekly Business Summary' (prompt summarises invoices). Both are paused and both carry _permissions: {write: true, delete: false} for team07.
- Invoices belong to the accounting app, which is 403 for this seat (Invoice.* is not in its tools/list).
- The seat's tools/list nevertheless offers on these records:
  - AgentTask.update with writable prompt, plan, persona_id, provider_id, user_id, notify_party_id, and the run-history fields last_run_status, last_run_at, last_run_error, last_run_error_kind, last_run_session_id, run_count.
  - AgentTask.resume (paused -> active) and AgentTask.run_now.
  - AgentTask.create accepting user_id, status and the same run-history fields.

Expected: a CRM seat cannot modify, resume or run another user's scheduled agent, least of all one that runs against an app the seat is denied. user_id (run-as identity) and run history (last_run_*, run_count) are server-owned and not writable by any client.

Impact: a CRM-seat agent (or a prompt-injected one) could replace the prompt of an agent that runs with accounting access, resume or run it, and make it run as another user; the forged run history would hide it. This is the AgentTask counterpart of the AgentSession findings already filed on Suryodaya (Bug 5: other teams' sessions writable; Bug 6: AgentSession.update exposes audit and billing fields).

Reproduce (read-only):
1. tools/list -> AgentTask.update / .resume / .run_now / .create are present; inspect AgentTask.update inputSchema.properties.
2. AgentTask.list {} -> 2 records, created_by c91dd152..., _permissions.write = true.

Scope checked: Suryodaya shows the same - all 96 AgentTask records (95 with created_by null, 82 paused) are flagged write: true to team07, and the same tools are offered. Not exercised on purpose: proving the write means editing another user's agent. AgentPersona, AgentSeat, AgentToolPolicy and AgentProvider are correctly read-only to this seat.

Related: Suryodaya Bug 5, Bug 6, Bug 17 (cross-team agent-governance write access).

Keystone MCP: 41 list tools publish create-time defaults on their FILTER parameters - a client that applies schema defaults gets Deal.list 177 -> 0 and Activity.list 321 -> 15, and Quotation.list rejects its own default (MEDIUM)

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in; also Suryodaya] MEDIUM - API contract. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline) with a READ-ONLY probe: tools/list and *.list calls only.

What happened:
In tools/list, 41 entity *.list tools declare JSON-Schema 'default' values on their filter parameters. The values are the create-time defaults copied into the list schema, for example:
- Activity.list: done=false, duration=30, priority='medium'
- Deal.list: stage='new', value=0, probability=0, currency='locale:base_currency'
- AgentTask.list: status='active'; AgentTodo.list: status='open'; SalesOrder.list: status='draft', date='today'
- Quotation.list: date='today', status='draft', currency_code='locale:base_currency'
The server applies no default when a filter is omitted, so a bare call is correct. But MCP clients and LLM tool callers routinely fill in schema defaults, and then silently receive a subset:

| Tool | no filters | with the declared defaults |
| Activity.list (Keystone / Suryodaya) | 321 / 181 | 15 / 23 |
| Deal.list (Keystone / Suryodaya) | 177 / 143 | 0 / 0 |
| AgentTask.list (Keystone) | 2 | 0 |

Two defaults are placeholders, not values:
- currency='locale:base_currency' matches nothing: Deal.list {currency:'USD'} -> 175, {currency:'locale:base_currency'} -> 0.
- Quotation.list rejects its own declared default: {date:'today'} -> -32602 '/date must be a valid date.' (same on Suryodaya).

Expected: filter parameters of list tools carry no default (limit, offset and sort_order are the only legitimate ones), and no placeholder token ever appears as a schema value.

Impact: the platform is built for agents, which read these schemas. An agent that honours the declared defaults reports 'no deals' or only 15 of 321 activities, with no error - a silently wrong answer.

Reproduce (read-only):
1. tools/list -> Deal.list inputSchema.properties.stage.default == 'new', value.default == 0, currency.default == 'locale:base_currency'.
2. Deal.list {} -> total 177. Deal.list {stage:'new', value:0, probability:0, currency:'locale:base_currency'} -> total 0.
3. Quotation.list {date:'today'} -> -32602.

Related: d54159a2 (sort_order replaced by the numeric column on Item/Pipeline/AddressBook) is a different defect in the same list-schema generation.

Keystone: company-wide CRM settings (CRMPreferences: deal_rot_days, default_currency, fiscal_year_start, lead assignment) are writable from an agent seat shared by several teams, and a second settings record can be created (MEDIUM)

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in; also Suryodaya] MEDIUM - governance / shared configuration. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline, role sales_user) with a READ-ONLY probe: tools/list and CRMPreferences.list only. Nothing was written.

What happened:
- There is one CRMPreferences record for the company (Keystone record created by user 70ea1138-2f4a-4bdb-b4dd-51a69ee4a9bd; deal_rot_days 30, default_currency USD, fiscal_year_start january). It carries _permissions.write: true for team07.
- The seat's tools/list offers CRMPreferences.update on deal_rot_days, default_currency, fiscal_year_start, auto_assign_leads, assignment_method, lead_score_threshold, lead_scoring_enabled, enable_web_to_lead, enable_email_tracking, default_deal_pipeline, reminder_before_hours.
- It also offers CRMPreferences.create, which would add a second, conflicting settings record for the same company.

Expected: tenant-wide configuration is changed by an admin (or through an approval), not by an agent seat whose book is shared with other teams; and there is at most one CRMPreferences record per company.

Impact: every team on the CRM book relies on these values - e.g. deal_rot_days is the documented rot threshold behind every team's rotting-deals answer, and default_currency / fiscal_year_start drive reporting. One seat's agent (or a prompt-injected one) could change them for all teams, silently.

Reproduce (read-only):
1. CRMPreferences.list {} -> 1 record, _permissions.write = true for a sales_user seat.
2. tools/list -> CRMPreferences.update and CRMPreferences.create present, with the fields above.

Scope checked: Suryodaya is the same (record created by 520e389e..., deal_rot_days 30, default_currency INR, fiscal_year_start april, write: true). Company, Pipeline, Goal and AgentToolPolicy are correctly read-only to this seat, so the CRM settings record is the odd one out. Not exercised on purpose: a write would change shared configuration for every team.

Related: the deal-rot threshold reports on Suryodaya (d8bfe59f, 41993336) - this is the same deal_rot_days value.

Suryodaya: 25 sales deals and 53 leads are placed on the company's own employees - 5 of them closed_won for Rs 3,990,593.64 (6% of all won value) - and nothing prevents a deal or lead sitting on a staff party (MEDIUM)

[Suryodaya, agentswitch.theschoolofai.in; platform rule also checked on Keystone] MEDIUM - data integrity. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline, role sales_user, user b0f54dbe) with a READ-ONLY scan of Party, Deal and Lead (MCP *.list), plus one probe on team07's own Keystone fixture.

What happened:
- 25 Deal records and 53 Lead records have a party_id whose ONLY role is 'employee' (roles = [{role: 'employee', active: true}]). These are the company's own staff, with @suryodaya.in email addresses - e.g. Sunil Shelke (sunil.shelke@suryodaya.in), Ramesh Barve, Dnyaneshwar Kharat, Anil Deshpande, Sneha Rao, Manoj Rokade.
- They are seed records: created 2026-09-12 by 'system' (13 deals) and user ae8cff28-f42f-4d4b-ad29-305fe1d3446a (12 deals, 53 leads). Many are the 'Deal from <party-uuid>' deals of report 92e9f861 (B4).
- 5 of these deals are closed_won, together Rs 3,990,593.64 - 6% of the book's Rs 62,303,179.65 won value:
  - 'Surface Plate - shift handover' Rs 2,128,495.38 (party Sunil Shelke)
  - 'Sangli despatch, week 19' Rs 999,148.75 (Anil Deshpande)
  - 'Quote - Vishwas Forgings Enterprises' Rs 465,512.92 (Dnyaneshwar Kharat)
  - 'Ahmednagad despatch, week 44' Rs 325,316.24 (Sneha Rao)
  - "Toolmaker's Vice - despatch hold" Rs 72,119.35 (Ramesh Barve)
  (A sixth won deal on an employee, 'T6-authtest-deal-statemachine', is another team's test.)
- Keystone has none in its seed, but the platform does not prevent it: on team07's own fixture party (Keystone, '[team07-test BH-20261013] H1 party', with an open deal) Party.update roles -> [{role:'employee'}] and -> [{role:'supplier'}] were both accepted with no warning (restored afterwards).

Expected: a sales Deal or Lead is placed on a customer/prospect party; assigning one to an employee-only party (or turning a party with open deals into an employee) is refused or at least flagged; the seed book does not book staff as customers.

Impact: won revenue, forecast, goal progress and every 'customers not contacted' list include the company's own staff. An agent asked which customers to call lists colleagues; won value is overstated by 6%.

Reproduce (read-only):
1. Party.list {limit:1000}; Deal.list {limit:1000}; Lead.list {limit:1000}.
2. Join Deal.party_id / Lead.party_id to Party; keep rows whose party roles are exactly ['employee'] -> 25 deals (stages: new 20, closed_won 6, closed_lost 4, incl. 1 test deal), 53 seed leads.

Related: 92e9f861 (B4, 'Deal from <uuid>' titles - largely these same deals); the malformed-pipeline seed reports.

Keystone: US sales tax ignores line discounts - a $139.40 quote is charged $14.72 Ohio tax (5.75% of the $256.06 pre-discount gross) instead of $8.02; a line discounted 100% is still taxed (HIGH)

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH (money). Reproduced 2026-10-13 via MCP Quotation.create on a team07 fixture: QTN-2026-00037, customer '[team07-test KS-BH-20260929] cust-OH' (billing Canton OH 44702), status draft. No items[].amount was sent - only qty, rate and discount.

What happened (7 lines, Ohio state rate 5.75%):
| qty | rate | discount % | stored amount |
| 3 | 0.335 | 0 | 1.00 |
| 0.5 | 10.01 | 0 | 5.00 |
| 1 | 100 | 100 | 0.00 |
| 7 | 0.01 | 0 | 0.07 |
| 2.5 | 19.99 | 33.33 | 33.32 |
| 1 | 0.005 | 0 | 0.01 |
| 3 | 33.333 | 0 | 100.00 |
- net_total 139.40 (= sum of stored line amounts, correct).
- taxes[0] 'Ohio State Sales Tax' rate 5.75, amount 14.72; grand_total 154.12.
- 5.75% x 139.40 = 8.02. But 5.75% x 256.059 = 14.72, where 256.059 is the sum of qty x rate with NO discount applied. The line discounted 100% (net 0.00) contributes $5.75 of tax; the 33.33% discount is ignored too.
- Overcharge on this order: $6.70 (83%).

Contrast: Suryodaya's GST engine applies the rate to the discounted line amount - checked on its 70 discounted quotations and 199 discounted sales orders (e.g. QTN-2026-00023: 18% of 199,356.86 = 35,884.23, the post-discount amount). So this is specific to the US sales-tax path.

Secondary, same document: line amounts are rounded with binary floating point, not decimal half-up - 3 x 0.335 = 1.005 -> 1.00 and 0.5 x 10.01 = 5.005 -> 5.00, but 1 x 0.005 -> 0.01. Each is a one-cent error in the line and net total.

Expected: the sales-tax base for each line is qty x rate x (1 - discount/100), i.e. the stored line amount; line amounts are rounded half-up in decimal.

Impact: every discounted quotation and sales order on the US tenant over-collects sales tax, and fully discounted (free) lines are taxed at list price.

Reproduce: Quotation.create {company_id, party_id (an OH-billed customer), items: [{qty:1, rate:100, discount:100}, {qty:1, rate:100, discount:0}]} -> expected net 100.00 / tax 5.75; this report predicts tax 11.50.

Related: 0349cde4 (tax computed from a client-supplied items[].amount). That needs a bad client value; this one happens with ordinary input and may share the engine's line-base calculation. Editing QTN-2026-00037 to a single line was not possible - engine-taxed quotes cannot be edited (filed earlier).

Suryodaya storefront charges 28% GST on items configured at GST 18% - Bench Vice 100mm (HSN 82055900) costs Rs 4,478.72 instead of Rs 4,128.82, for every shipping state (HIGH)

[Suryodaya, agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH (money). Reproduced 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline) with two storefront checkouts, both abandoned immediately (status cancelled, no SalesOrder created).

What happened:
- Item 'SuryaTools Bench Vice 100mm' (e7e982cd-dd11-4f31-b912-3f0a9903f6ed, ITEM-2026-00046, HSN 82055900, selling_price 3499.00) is configured intra_state_tax = 'GST 18%' and inter_state_tax = 'GST 18%'.
- endpoint.storefront.checkout, 1 x this item, no coupon, no shipping charge:
  - WEB-2026-00112, ship to Pune, Maharashtra 411001: subtotal 3499.00, tax_amount 979.72, grand_total 4478.72.
  - WEB-2026-00113, ship to Ahmedabad, Gujarat 380001: identical - tax_amount 979.72, grand_total 4478.72.
  - 979.72 / 3499.00 = 28%. At the configured 18% the tax is 629.82 and the total 4128.82: the shopper is overcharged Rs 349.90 (8.5% of the price).
- The paid storefront order already in the book shows the same: SO-2026-00238 (another team's '[TEST a08] checkout', 2026-10-08) records CGST 14% 489.86 + SGST 14% 489.86, with place_of_supply null.
- Every seeded sales order for the same item charges CGST 9% + SGST 9% (5 orders) - only the storefront path uses 28%.

Likely cause (hypothesis): Item.intra_state_tax / inter_state_tax hold only a label ('GST 18%'); the numeric intra_state_tax_rate / inter_state_tax_rate are null on all 11 published items (and on 32 other items hold rupee amounts such as 330245.65 instead of a percentage). The storefront appears to fall back to a 28% default when the numeric rate is missing.

Also observed (same as Keystone G10): payment.verify {outcome: 'abandoned'} returns an error ('That payment was not completed', 422 payment_not_completed) although the order is cancelled as requested.

Expected: the storefront taxes each line at the item's configured GST rate (18% here), split CGST+SGST for a Maharashtra destination and IGST for other states, and records the place of supply on the resulting SalesOrder.

Impact: every consumer buying a published item on the web store is overcharged by 10 percentage points of GST, and the order is booked with tax the company would have to refund or remit wrongly.

Reproduce: endpoint.storefront.checkout {customer_name, customer_email, shipping_address, shipping_city, shipping_state:'Maharashtra', shipping_pincode:'411001', items:[{item_id:'e7e982cd-dd11-4f31-b912-3f0a9903f6ed', qty:1}]} -> totals.tax_amount 979.72. Then payment.verify {order_id, order_token, outcome:'abandoned'} to cancel.

Suryodaya: 15 inter-state sales orders carry CGST+SGST instead of IGST (Rs 207,976.69 under the wrong tax head), an intra-state order carries IGST, and on 87 orders CGST and SGST differ by Rs 0.01 (MEDIUM)

[Suryodaya, agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM - GST compliance / data integrity. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline) with a READ-ONLY audit of all 313 SalesOrders (MCP SalesOrder.list).

The company's home state is Maharashtra (27). Under GST, a supply whose place of supply is another state is inter-state and attracts IGST; CGST+SGST apply only when the place of supply is Maharashtra. A supply to an SEZ is always inter-state.

What happened:
1. 15 confirmed orders with an inter-state place_of_supply carry CGST 9% + SGST 9% and no IGST - Rs 207,976.69 of tax under the wrong head: 24-Gujarat 8, 29-Karnataka 4, 23-Madhya Pradesh 3 (gst_treatment consumer 12, business_gst 2, sez 1). Largest: SO-2026-00059 (24-Gujarat, business_gst) Rs 94,752.28; SO-2026-00060 (29-Karnataka, SEZ) Rs 66,110.33. Full list: SO-2026-00060, 00059, 00058, 00226, 00229, 00233, 00232, 00122, 00113, 00104, 00095, SO-2025-00037, 00028, 00019, 00010. The consumer orders' parties have shipping addresses in those same states.
2. SO-2026-00056 (place_of_supply 27-Maharashtra, business_gst) carries IGST 18% Rs 139,515.80 instead of CGST+SGST.
3. On 87 orders the CGST and SGST rows differ by exactly Rs 0.01 (e.g. SO-2026-00060: CGST 33,055.16 / SGST 33,055.17), because the total is rounded and then split; each half should be computed and rounded on its own, so the two are always equal.

All of these are seeded history (created_by 520e389e or null). Arithmetic is otherwise clean: line amount = qty x rate x (1 - discount), sum of lines = net_total, grand_total = net + taxes on every order.

Expected: tax head follows place_of_supply (and SEZ treatment); CGST = SGST on every intra-state order.

Impact: GST returns built from this book would report tax to the wrong government (state vs centre) for Rs 3.5 lakh of tax; any agent or report summing IGST vs CGST/SGST is wrong.

Reproduce (read-only): SalesOrder.list {limit:1000}; for each order compare place_of_supply's state code with the tax_type of its taxes[] rows.

Related: the storefront GST rate report filed today (28% on an 18% item), whose resulting order SO-2026-00238 also records CGST+SGST with no place_of_supply.

Suryodaya: quotation tax data is internally inconsistent - total_tax disagrees with taxes[] on 35 quotes (e.g. Rs 229,116.02 vs Rs 1,225.31), tax rows are named after products or unnamed, reverse-charge quotes still collect tax, place_of_supply has two formats (MEDIUM)

[Suryodaya, agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM - data integrity. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline) with a READ-ONLY audit of all 103 Quotations (MCP Quotation.list).

What happened:
1. On 35 quotations total_tax does not equal the sum of taxes[].amount; grand_total follows total_tax, so taxes[] is the wrong one. Example QTN-2026-00023: net 1,809,621.81, total_tax 229,116.02, grand 2,038,737.83, but taxes[] = [('Pipe Wrench 9533', 9%, 126.60), (null, 9%, 1,098.71)] = 1,225.31.
2. taxes[].tax_type is null on 81 rows and a product name on about 70 rows ('Pipe Wrench 9533', 'V-Block Pair 9583', 'Bench Vice 9584', ...); only 26 rows name a tax (CGST/SGST/IGST).
3. 14 quotations have is_reverse_charge = 1 yet carry tax charged by the supplier (e.g. QTN-2026-00024 unregistered_business, tax 1,963.52; QTN-2026-00026 business_gst, 1,355.22). Under reverse charge the recipient pays the tax; the supplier's document should carry none.
4. place_of_supply is stored in two formats: 63 quotations use a bare state name ('Karnataka', 'West Bengal'), while sales orders and 13 quotations use the 'NN-State' code ('27-Maharashtra'). The tax head cannot be derived reliably from the bare form.
5. 15 quotations charge tax with no place_of_supply at all.
All affected quotations are seeded (created_by ae8cff28-f42f-4d4b-ad29-305fe1d3446a). Line arithmetic is clean (amount = qty x rate x (1 - discount); sum of lines = net_total).

Expected: one tax total per document that equals its tax rows; tax rows name the tax (CGST/SGST/IGST/cess); reverse-charge documents carry no supplier-collected tax; place_of_supply in one format with the state code.

Impact: any agent or report reading a quotation's tax gets two different answers (totals differ by up to 185x); quote-to-order conversion and GST reporting inherit the inconsistency.

Reproduce (read-only): Quotation.list {limit:1000}; compare total_tax with sum(taxes[].amount); inspect taxes[].tax_type and place_of_supply.

Related: Bug 22 (two validity dates disagree on the same quotations) - a different field on the same seeded quotation set.

Suryodaya: the AgentTask scheduler silently runs tasks that have no schedule every 60 minutes - a 'Weekly' task fired 226 times in 9.5 days - and kept firing for 10 days although every one of the 1,209 scheduled jobs failed (MEDIUM)

[Suryodaya, agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM - scheduler correctness / runaway jobs. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline) with a READ-ONLY probe: AgentTask.list, AgentJob.list (all 1,209 jobs) and AgentFloorConfig.list. Nothing written.

What happened:
1. The schedule fields are missing on many tasks: all 36 tasks with schedule_type 'cron' have cron_expression = null, and 8 tasks with schedule_type 'interval' have interval_minutes = null.
2. Such tasks still run - every 60 minutes. Gaps between consecutive jobs (AgentJob.trigger_id = the task), 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-22:
| Task | schedule_type | cron_expression | interval_minutes | jobs | median gap |
| Weekly overdue invoice reminder - Stores | cron | null | null | 226 | 60.1 min |
| Supplier delivery follow-up - Assembly | cron | null | 28 | 226 | 60.1 min |
| Open ticket digest - Machining | cron | null | 39 | 227 | 60.1 min |
| Supplier delivery follow-up - Stores | interval | null | null | 226 | 60.1 min |
| Morning production summary - Paint Shop (control) | interval | null | 45 | 299 | 45.0 min |
The control task with a real interval keeps its 45-minute cadence, so the 60-minute rate is a silent fallback for a missing schedule. A task named 'Weekly' ran about 168 times more often than intended.
3. No failure stop: all 1,209 AgentJob rows in the book have status 'failed' (error 'agent_authority_unresolved' 773, 'Gemini rejected the request (HTTP 400)' 328, 'This job requires a plan before execution' 107). Each task has max_retries 3, yet the five recurring tasks above each failed 226-299 times in a row and kept firing hourly until they were paused on 2026-09-22 (updated_by null).
4. AgentTask.run_count does not match the job history on 27 of 96 tasks (e.g. 'Supplier delivery follow-up - Press Shop' run_count 655 with 0 jobs; 'Supplier delivery follow-up - Assembly' 277 vs 226 jobs) - possibly seeded values, but the counter cannot be trusted as a run history.

Expected: a cron task without cron_expression (or an interval task without interval_minutes) is rejected when saved, or at least never scheduled, rather than defaulting to hourly; a recurring task that keeps failing is paused after its retry budget instead of firing hundreds of times; run_count equals the number of runs recorded.

Impact: misconfigured scheduled agents run up to 168x their intended rate, and a broken one keeps consuming the job queue (global_concurrency 4 in AgentFloorConfig) indefinitely. With a working provider each of those runs would also cost LLM tokens.

Reproduce (read-only): AgentTask.list {limit:1000} -> count schedule_type='cron' with cron_expression null; AgentJob.list {limit:1000, offset 0..1000} -> group by trigger_id, sort created_at, compute gaps.

Related: Bug 9 (e316d680) - scheduled jobs run under personas whose system_prompt is filler text; this report is about the scheduler's handling of the schedule itself.

Keystone: manufacturing.demand_forecast drops every overdue open sales-order line from open demand - it reports 0 open units while 13 open lines (5,180 units) are past their delivery date (MEDIUM-HIGH)

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in; also Suryodaya] MEDIUM-HIGH - planning data loss. Found 2026-10-13 by team07 (seat 07 Pipeline) with a READ-ONLY probe: endpoint.manufacturing.demand_forecast and SalesOrder.list. Nothing written.

What happened:
- endpoint.manufacturing.demand_forecast (generated_for 2026-10-13, horizon_months 3) documents its open demand as: "non-cancelled SalesOrder lines' qty - delivered_qty, bucketed by delivery_date, else expected_shipment_date, else the order date".
- Keystone result: counts.open_demand_units 0.0, open_lines 0, open_orders 0; every item's forecast_periods carry open_demand_qty 0.
- Recomputing that exact basis from SalesOrder.list (all 171 orders): 13 non-cancelled lines on 13 orders still have qty - delivered_qty > 0, totalling 5,180 units - and every one has a delivery date before 2026-10, i.e. it is overdue.
- So only lines whose bucket falls inside the horizon (2026-10 to 2026-12) are counted; overdue lines fall into no bucket and disappear.
- Suryodaya shows the same: forecast open_lines 1, open_demand_units 1.0 (while also saying open_orders 9), against 512 open lines on 294 orders totalling 71,616 units with delivery dates before 2026-10 (endpoint.make.orders lists 543 open lines there).

Expected: open demand that is already late is carried into the first forecast period (or reported separately as backlog), never dropped. The counts (open_orders / open_lines / open_demand_units) should agree with each other and with make.orders.

Impact: the forecast tells production planning there is nothing left to build exactly when the backlog is largest; overdue customer orders - the most urgent demand - are invisible to anyone (or any agent) planning from this endpoint. Combined with make.orders reporting late=false on overdue lines (our report K3), two planning views hide the same late work.

Reproduce (read-only):
1. endpoint.manufacturing.demand_forecast {} -> counts.open_demand_units.
2. SalesOrder.list {limit:1000}; for non-cancelled orders sum items[].qty - delivered_qty where > 0, bucketing by delivery_date / expected_shipment_date / date.
3. Compare: Keystone 0 vs 5,180 units (all before 2026-10).

Related: K3 (make.orders late=false on overdue lines); Bug 16/19 concern the CRM /api/forecast, a different endpoint.
